item.description: arXiv:2608.17493v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: By means of the theory of compound (non-homogeneous) Poisson processes we define a general framework which includes most of the generalizations of the Poisson processes, both in the Skellam sense and in the space-fractional sense. We prove that Bernstein subordination is the only time change that leads to a compound Poisson process. We also consider the case of subordination with inverse Bernstein subordinators. Then, we focus on the integrals of compound processes. We give an explicit representation of the fractional integral of a compound Poisson process, showing that for fixed $t$ it is distributed as a compound Poisson random variable. We then extend this result to more general integral forms. Furthermore, we obtain some limit results, explicit forms of the iterated integrals and their governing equation. Finally, we study the integral of compound renewal processes in the Fourier-Laplace domain.
item.dc:creator: Fabrizio Cinque, Enzo Orsingher

item.title: Universal existence and generic uniqueness for quadratic BSDE systems in a two-player stochastic differential game
item.description: arXiv:2609.29762v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study two-dimensional quadratic backward stochastic differential equations in the augmented natural filtration of a one-dimensional Brownian motion. The generator has components $q_{\theta,i}(z)=z_i(z_1+z_2)-\alpha_i z_i^2/2$, $i=1,2$, where $\theta=(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)\in\mathbb{R}^2$. In the associated stochastic differential game, two players choose efforts $u_1,u_2$, the common state has drift $u_1+u_2$, and player $i$ pays $u_i^2/2$ per unit time and has risk sensitivity $\alpha_i-1$. For every bounded terminal payoff vector $\xi$, which may depend on the entire state path, $(Y,Z)\mapsto Z$ is a bijection from solutions in $\mathcal{S}^\infty\times\mathrm{BMO}$ to Nash equilibria in BMO controls. Whether the risk-neutral system ($\alpha_1=\alpha_2=1$) is well posed for every such $\xi$ was left open in [Jackson (2023), Section 6.4]. For $\alpha_1\alpha_2\ne0$ with $\alpha_1^{-1}+\alpha_2^{-1}=1$, existence and uniqueness in $\mathcal{S}^\infty\times\mathrm{BMO}$ for every bounded $\xi$ were established in [Fan, Hu and Tang (2025), Corollary 2.25]. We prove that every bounded $\xi$ admits a solution in $\mathcal{S}^\infty\times\mathrm{BMO}$ for every $\theta\in\mathbb{R}^2$. The solution is unique for every bounded $\xi$ if $(\alpha_1-1)(\alpha_2-1)=1$, but for every $\theta$ with $(\alpha_1-1)(\alpha_2-1)\ne1$, we construct a bounded $\xi$ admitting at least two distinct solutions in $\mathcal{S}^\infty\times\mathrm{BMO}$. Nevertheless, for each $\theta\in\mathbb{R}^2$ and $M>0$, uniqueness holds on a dense $G_\delta$ subset of the space of $[-M,M]^2$-valued terminal conditions equipped with the topology of convergence in probability. Moreover, if $\xi_n$ in this space converges in probability to a point $\xi$ of this subset, every choice of solutions for $\xi_n$ converges to the unique solution for $\xi$ in $\mathcal{S}^p\times\mathcal{H}^p$ for every $1\le p<\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Siyi Wang

item.title: Seed thresholds and degree variance in heterogeneous bootstrap percolation with growing degrees
item.description: arXiv:2610.04420v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study bootstrap percolation with independent vertex thresholds taking values one and two, with threshold-one probability $(1-c/d)/d$ for fixed $c>0$. The seed set is chosen uniformly among sets of a prescribed deterministic size, independently of the graph and thresholds. We prove threshold statements at fixed relative margins. For uniform simple graphs with prescribed nonnegative integer degrees of even sum and exact mean $d$, assume $\max_i|d_i-d|\le C\sqrt d$ and $c+1-v_n\ge\kappa>0$, where $v_n=\operatorname{Var}(D)/d$ and $C,\kappa$ are fixed. When $d\to\infty$ and $d=o(n^{1/7})$, the leading seed scale is $n(c+1-v_n)^2/(2d^4)$, without requiring a limit of $v_n$. At fixed relative margins below and above this scale, the final active set has size $O(n/d^3)$ and $n-o(n)$, respectively, with high probability. For regular graphs, the supercritical conclusion strengthens to full activation. For $G(n,d/n)$, the same $O(n/d^3)$ and $n-o(n)$ conclusions hold when $d\to\infty$ and $d^5/n\to0$, with seed scale $nc^2/(2d^4)$. Thus regular and independent-edge graphs have different coefficients at the same asymptotic mean degree. Local exploration estimates yield explicit inactive remainders and survive conditioning on simplicity in the prescribed model. We also quantify the precision obstruction to static inclusion transfer and compute deterministic response-barrier corrections, without identifying a shrinking random critical window. A separate appendix gives the corresponding fixed-margin terminal bounds for iid thresholds of fixed bounded support, with unchanged threshold-one probability and threshold-two mass bounded away from zero.
item.dc:creator: Aleksandr Rodionov

item.title: Cutoff beyond non-negative curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.26019v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study how a relaxed gradient estimate is enough to prove cutoff for several new families of Markov processes, within the varentropy framework of [Sal25]. In particular, we show how certain regularization estimates from hypocoercivity theory allow one to prove cutoff for kinetic dynamics. Moreover, we prove cutoff for some families of diffusions with non-convex potentials and for mean-field dynamics, as well as for biased random walks on the symmetric group, giving a simple proof of a far-reaching extension of a result of [NY24].
item.dc:creator: Max Fathi, Arnaud Guillin, Cyril Labb\'e, Justin Salez

item.title: Coexistence and extinction in stochastic Lotka--Volterra systems with Volterra--Lyapunov stable interactions
item.description: arXiv:2610.28174v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider stochastic Lotka-Volterra systems $dX=\mathrm{Diag}(X)(\alpha+AX)dt+\mathrm{Diag}(X)\Gamma\,dB$ with nondegenerate noise and a Volterra-Lyapunov stable interaction matrix $A$, that is, $DA+A^\top D\prec0$ for some positive diagonal matrix $D$. This class covers every self-limited predator-prey food web that is conservative in the sense of Volterra, in particular every such web whose interaction graph is a forest. Let $\beta=\alpha-\frac12\mathrm{diag}(\Gamma\Gamma^\top)$ be the vector of noise-corrected growth rates and $m=-A^{-1}\beta$. We show that the process has a stationary distribution under which all species have positive densities if and only if $m>0$. In that case the process is strongly stochastically persistent, and its stationary distribution is unique and has mean $m$. When $m>0$ fails, the species that survive are those present in the unique saturated nonnegative equilibrium $\bar x$ of the deterministic system $\dot x=\mathrm{Diag}(x)(\beta+Ax)$. Almost surely, the occupation measures converge to the stationary distribution of this subcommunity, and $\log X_i(t)/t$ converges to $(\beta+A\bar x)_i\le0$ for every species $i$. The proofs rely on the theory of invasion rates of Hening and Nguyen. For Lotka-Volterra systems, invasion rates are affine in the mean of the underlying measure. Combined with two quadratic identities, this provides explicit weights $Dm$ for their persistence theorem and identifies the limiting regime when persistence fails, without enumerating the invariant measures on the boundary.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Ramirez Osorio

item.title: The Martingale Property in Volterra Volatility Models
item.description: arXiv:2610.32684v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study martingality and strict local martingality in a broad class of stochastic and path-dependent Volterra volatility models and explain the underlying mechanisms. Our martingality criteria allow rough kernels and rely on non-accessibility of an explosive direction or one-sided growth bounds on the Girsanov drift. For smooth kernels, we derive sufficient conditions for strict local martingality from an explosion criterion allowing multiplicative noise, coupled factors and general initial input curves. Our results recover classical criteria and yield new results for Volterra and path-dependent models.
item.dc:creator: Julien Guyon, Thibault Jeannin, Benjamin Jourdain

item.title: Diffusion-limited aggregation: Boundary, vacancies and shape exclusion
item.description: arXiv:2610.37625v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For external Diffusion-Limited Aggregation (DLA) on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with $d \geq 2$, we prove that the number of boundary edges grows linearly. Consequently, a positive fraction of the aggregate lies outside every compact region rescaled to have volume equal to the number of particles. We also show that the probability that the limiting aggregate covers more than a $1-\alpha$ fraction of a cube decays exponentially in its volume for some $\alpha>0$. For Euclidean DLA in every dimension $d \geq 2$, we show that each particle has approximately two near neighbors on average. We then deduce that a positive fraction of the planar Euclidean DLA particles lie outside any compact region scaled to the optimal sphere packing volume.
item.dc:creator: Amir Dembo, Matthew Junge

item.title: Generalized Wishart processes under nonlinear expectation
item.description: arXiv:2611.02728v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a theory of generalized Wishart processes within the framework of $G$-expectation, with $G$-Dyson Brownian motion and the $G$-Wishart process as two typical examples. In contrast to the classical setting, we show that $G$-Dyson Brownian motion may exhibit collisions and provide a sufficient condition ensuring the non-collision property of the eigenvalues of generalized Wishart processes. We then derive the equations governing the high-dimensional limits of the empirical spectral measures under $G$-expectation, leading to the corresponding semicircle law for $G$-Dyson Brownian motion and Marchenko--Pastur law for the $G$-Wishart process.
item.dc:creator: Xinpeng Li, Yiran Mi, Jian Song, Shuzhen Yang

item.title: Recurrence and Transience in Monotone Environments: Increasing Conductances and Growing Domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.15999v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study discrete-time random walks on a locally finite graph whose conductances are non-decreasing in time and bounded on each edge. We compare its hitting probabilities with those of the homogeneous walk whose conductances are fixed at the starting time. These estimates give another proof of two results of Li and Park, who work under more general assumptions. If the upper network is recurrent, the walk visits every vertex infinitely often almost surely. If the initial network is transient, the expected number of visits to each vertex is finite. Let us first consider the probability of leaving a finite set before hitting a given vertex. The difference between this probability and its value for the frozen walk is bounded in absolute value by the square root of the product of a capacity increment and a dual energy. On an initially transient network, we obtain a lower bound on the probability of never hitting the vertex. Both proofs use a comparison of two Dirichlet forms and a contraction property of the killed transition operators. We also consider walks on increasing finite sets. On each prescribed time interval, called a plateau, the transition operator is fixed. A lower bound on transition probabilities after mixing and an upper bound on the expected number of returns give a sufficient condition for every vertex to be visited infinitely often almost surely. For uniformly elliptic lazy walks on boxes of radius $R_n$ in $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d\geq3$, it is enough that $\sum_n(L_n-b_n)_+/R_n^d$ diverges, where $L_n$ is the duration of the $n$th plateau and $b_n=\lceil aR_n^2\rceil$ for a constant $a$ depending only on the dimension and the ellipticity bound.
item.dc:creator: Nordine Anis Moumeni

item.title: Asymptotic analysis of infinite-server queues driven by a Cox process with squared Bessel arrival intensity
item.description: arXiv:2611.16195v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper introduces a model for infinite-server queues driven by a Cox process with stochastic intensity given by a squared Bessel (BESQ) process. Exploiting the affine structure of the underlying dynamics, we derive a closed-form expression for the joint moment-generating function (MGF) of the arrival intensity, the number of customers in the system, and the integral of the number of customers in the system over a time interval. The asymptotic properties of the model are also analysed. We establish laws of large numbers, central limit theorems, large deviation principles, and moderate deviation principles for several quantities of interest. More precisely, these results are obtained for three important settings: cumulative occupancy over a finite time interval, system occupancy under a diverging long-run mean arrival intensity, and the superposition of independent infinite-server queues with Cox-BESQ arrival intensities. Numerical experiments illustrate the associated rate functions and demonstrate the effectiveness of the resulting rare-event approximations.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Da Fonseca, Yajun Shi, Wenjun Zhang

item.title: Tight Lipschitz Hardness for Solving Random Polynomial Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.28390v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the problem of solving $n$ polynomial equations in $d$ real variables: $F_1({\boldsymbol x})=0, \ldots, F_n({\boldsymbol x})=0$, with unknowns ${\boldsymbol x}=(x_1, \ldots, x_d)$ satisfying the normalization constraint $\|{\boldsymbol x}\|=1$, when the polynomials are i.i.d. realization of a rotationally invariant Gaussian process. In previous work (Montanari, Subag, 2023), we developed an iterative algorithm that attempts to minimize the energy function $H({\boldsymbol x})=\|{\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x})\|^2/2$ (with ${\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x})=(F_i({\boldsymbol x}):i\le n)$), using first and second order information (gradient and Hessian of $H$) at a sequence of query points ${\boldsymbol x}_1, \ldots, {\boldsymbol x}_k$. Here, we prove a lower bound on the minimum energy achieved by any algorithm that is Lipschitz continuous in the coefficients of the polynomials $F_i$. We prove that the lower bound matches the the energy achieved by the algorithm in (Montanari, Subag, 2023), hence characterizing the degree of accuracy to which the system of equations ${\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x})={\boldsymbol 0}$ can be solved by Lipschitz algorithms. Our results imply that, for certain choices of the distribution of the polynomials $F_i$, solutions exist with high probability but Lipschitz algorithms fails to find near-solutions, even in a very weak sense. Namely, if ${\boldsymbol x}^{alg}$ is the output of a Lipschitz algorithm, then $\|{\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x}^{alg})\|^2\ge \varepsilon {\mathbb E}[\|{\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x}_0)\|^2]$ (for ${\boldsymbol x}_0$ a non-random point on the unit sphere) with high probability for some $\varepsilon>0$. The proof is based on techniques developed in the context of spin glass theory.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Montanari, Eliran Subag

item.title: On $\beta=6$ Tracy-Widom distribution and the second Calogero-Painlev\'e system
item.description: arXiv:2010.06733v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Calogero-Painlev\'e systems were introduced in 2001 by K. Takasaki as a natural generalization of the classical Painlev\'e equations to the case of the several Painlev\'e ``particles'' coupled via the Calogero type interactions. In 2014, I. Rumanov discovered the remarkable fact that a particular case of the second Calogero-Painlev\'e II equation describes the Tracy-Widom distribution function for the general beta-ensembles with even values of the parameter beta. Most recently, in 2017 work of M. Bertola, M. Cafasso, and V. Rubtsov, it was proven that all Calogero-Painlev\'e systems are Lax integrable, and hence their solutions admit a Riemann-Hilbert representation. This important observation has opened the door to rigorous, based on the Deift-Zhou nonlinear steepest descent method, asymptotic analysis of the Calogero-Painlev\'e equations. This in turn yields the possibility of rigorous evaluation of the asymptotic behavior of the Tracy-Widom distributions for the values of beta beyond the classical $\beta =1, 2, 4.$ In this work we shall start an asymptotic analysis of the Calogero-Painlev\'e system with a special focus on the Calogero-Painlev\'e system corresponding to $\beta = 6$ Tracy-Widom distribution function. The principle technical challenge is the implementation of the nonlinear steepest descent approach beyond the $2\times 2$ matrix dimension of the corresponding Riemann-Hilbert problem; in our case, it is $6\times 6$.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Its, Andrei Prokhorov

item.title: Large-time behavior and accuracy of the Mean-Field Ensemble Kalman Filter in the Linear Detectable Setting
item.description: arXiv:2606.07729v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF), originally developed in the geophysical sciences, is now widely used for state and parameter estimation problems in various domains of application, and in particular in high dimensional settings. It may be viewed as a robust, cheap-to-implement,alternative to the optimal, Bayesian, filter. However, despite its empirical successes, theoretical understanding of its properties, in relation to the optimal filter, is in its infancy. We contribute novel theoretical understanding, studying the behavior of the EnKF in the infinite particle number setting; this is known as the mean-field ensemble Kalman filter (MFEnKF). In the linear setting with Gaussian noise and Gaussian initial data the MFEnKF coincides with the optimal filter, which is characterized by the Kalman filter. Our focus in this paper will be the linear setting with Gaussian noise, but with non-Gaussian initial data. Under the assumptions of nondegeneracy of the signal noise and detectability of the signal-observation pair we make three specific contributions, studying both discrete and continuous formulations of the methodology. First, in discrete time, we derive the MFEnKF via a variational approximation of the Bayes update using a covariance-weighted optimal transport metric. Secondly, we use this metric to show that the MFEnKF is a strict contraction towards the subspace of Gaussian measures, giving explicit geometric rates in terms of the covariances, in both discrete and continuous time. Finally, in the continuous-time setting, we deduce a stable form of almost sure accuracy of the MFEnKF: given any pair of initial laws (satisfying mild conditions) for the MFEnKF and the optimal filter, the 2-Wasserstein distance between their distributions decays exponentially, for almost every observation path.
item.dc:creator: Franca Hoffmann, Sangmin Park, Andrew M. Stuart

item.title: When Hedging Changes the Payoff: Option Replication with Price Impact and Execution Costs
item.description: arXiv:2609.36257v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Hedging a derivative by trading the underlying asset changes the payoff that the hedging intended to replicate. We study this phenomenon when trading generates price impact and execution costs. In a binomial model, we characterize replication through a fixed point equation. In continuous time, we derive a nonlinear pricing PDE whose implicit terminal condition captures the nature of the moving target problem of the hedger. For monotone convex Lipschitz payoffs (such as calls and puts) we establish exact replication under midpoint execution costs. Numerical experiments illustrate: (i) how price impact shifts the effective strike, (ii) the nonlinear dependence of the option price on the number of contracts, (iii) how execution costs smooth terminal holdings, (iv) the extent to which the hedger's own trading can bring an otherwise worthless option into the money, and (v) how the spread and the shape of the limit order book in the options market arise from the price impact and the shape of the limit order book of the underlying. In particular, calibrating the one-period binomial model to trade and quote data on near-expiry SPY call options, we find that our model explains 85\% of the observed option bid-ask spread for near-the-money options.
item.dc:creator: David Itkin, Leandro S\'anchez-Betancourt
